I wrote `src/test/java/org/apache/commons/lang3/builder/DiffBuilderAgentTest.java`, a self-contained JUnit 5 test class (matching the project's JUnit version, 5.14.4, and existing lambda/diamond-operator style under `--release 8`).

Coverage includes: all primitive and primitive-array `append` overloads (boolean/byte/char/double/float/int/long/short and their arrays), the `Object`/`Object[]` overload's runtime dispatch to the correct array-type overload (including null-left and non-primitive array cases), `double`/`float` NaN and signed-zero bit-level equality semantics, `append(String, DiffResult)` nesting/field-name prefixing and its NPE contract, the trivially-equal short-circuit (`==` and `.equals`), `setTestObjectsEquals(false)` overriding that short-circuit, the `Builder` API (defaults for null style/format, fluent chaining, NPE when left/right unset), `DiffResult`/`Diff` observable state (`getNumberOfDiffs`, `getDiffs` immutability, `toString` formatting, `Diff.toString`, `Diff.setValue` throwing), and the cycle-protection registry that prevents stack overflow when an object's `equals()` re-enters `DiffBuilder` construction for the same pair.

All 53 test methods pass — I didn't find a genuine bug in `DiffBuilder`. I deliberately did not assert on one edge case that looks like a javadoc overstatement (every `append` method's Javadoc unconditionally says it throws `NullPointerException` for a null field name, but the code only validates the field name lazily, when a `Diff` actually needs to be created): this is a standard lazy-validation pattern consistent with the rest of the class's design (skip all side effects, including validation, when values are trivially equal), not a functional defect, so I did not write a failing test for it.
